question: A seller allows a discount of 9% on a watch. If he allows a discount of 6%, he earns Rs. 30 more in profit. What is the marked price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in the given discount percentages = 9% − 6% = 3%

The difference in profit corresponds exactly to the difference in the discount amount.

⇒ 3% of Marked Price = Rs. 30

⇒ Marked Price = 30 × (100 ÷ 3) = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Discount = 9%

New Discount = 6%

Increase in profit = Rs. 30

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) − Discount

Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price (CP)

 
 
•

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Marked Price = MP and Cost Price = CP

⇒ Selling Price in Case 1 (SP₁) = MP − 9% of MP = 0.91 MP

⇒ Profit in Case 1 = 0.91 MP − CP

⇒ Selling Price in Case 2 (SP₂) = MP − 6% of MP = 0.94 MP

⇒ Profit in Case 2 = 0.94 MP − CP

⇒ Difference in profit = Profit in Case 2 − Profit in Case 1

⇒ (0.94 MP − CP) − (0.91 MP − CP) = 30

⇒ 0.03 MP = 30

⇒ MP = 30 ÷ 0.03 = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is an allowance given to the buyer on the catalog price. It is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. Selling Price = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single effective discount is calculated using the formula: (a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

Profit and Loss Baseline

Unlike discounts which are based on Marked Price, profit or loss is inherently always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise.
